verdict.root_cause: Not established. The only positive signal in the entire dispatch set is that productcatalogservice emitted STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on roughly 0–11.4% of its calls across the 15-minute window, intermittently rather than continuously, while continuing to serve the large majority of traffic (tr_839eda652d8a, tr_1096f7dba2d7). Every attempt to characterize the mechanism behind those errors failed to return data: no latency, CPU, memory, GC, thread or connection-pool series were ever queried or returned for productcatalogservice (tr_839eda652d8a, tr_1096f7dba2d7); both log dispatches ran against a hyphenated label value that matches no stream and were never re-run with the correct selector, so no error signature and no first-anomalous-line timestamp exist (tr_223ade85cee8, tr_f32b98c26f6e); and the two peer services examined, adservice and cartservice, returned no series at all — numerator and denominator both absent — which is a gap in instrumentation or traffic rather than a measurement of health (tr_ea2d754fc52d, tr_dc3105edf015). The change log is empty for productcatalogservice, but only over 04:43:15–04:58:15, and it was never extended to the preceding hour or to any dependency (tr_8c5b0d29808f, tr_227ccdd76acc). A partial, oscillating error rate with a healthy success majority is compatible with a saturating resource, a slow downstream whose calls time out on some fraction of requests, or a bad artifact on a subset of replicas; nothing in the collected evidence discriminates among these. Naming a class here would be guessing dressed as a finding.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent metric dispatches agree on the shape of the symptom: productcatalogservice is partially and intermittently failing, peaking near 11.4% of calls, with the denominator populated throughout (tr_839eda652d8a, tr_1096f7dba2d7). That shape rules out several things and both specialists said so — it is not a hard-down service or crash loop, not a chronic baseline, not a single discrete spike, and not upstream black-holing, since mixed-status call records are reaching instrumentation (tr_1096f7dba2d7). What it does not do is identify a mechanism. The four dispatch classes that would have discriminated all came back empty or misdirected. Both log queries used a selector that matches no stream, and the second specialist was explicit that the corrected re-run did not actually execute, so the emptiness carries no information about whether the service was logging (tr_223ade85cee8, tr_f32b98c26f6e) — this forecloses reading silence as a crash signal. Both change dispatches returned nothing, which does legitimately exclude a deploy, config edit, flag flip or in-window rollback landing on productcatalogservice between 04:43 and 04:58 (tr_8c5b0d29808f, tr_227ccdd76acc); it does not exclude a change earlier in the unqueried 03:53–04:43 interval, nor any change to a dependency, and both specialists flagged that limitation themselves. The absence of change evidence is therefore weak negative evidence against bad_deploy and bad_config in the immediate window, not affirmative evidence for any other class. The adservice and cartservice results are not clean bills of health: with the all-status denominator missing, the correct reading is that instrumentation or traffic stopped, which is itself an unexplained anomaly worth chasing rather than a reason to exclude those services (tr_ea2d754fc52d, tr_dc3105edf015). The retrieved ad-memory-squeeze incident is a tempting fit — intermittent frontend errors with the true culprit showing flat metrics — but adopting it would mean importing a memory-exhaustion mechanism that no dispatch in this investigation measured, and the corpus records what a responder saw then, not what is true now. The triage note that an unmeasured edge was crossed reinforces that the causal path leaves the instrumented region. Since resource_exhaustion, dependency_latency and bad_deploy each remain live and none has affirmative support, the class is unknown and no remediation follows from the evidence in hand.
open_questions: What do productcatalogservice's logs actually say? Both log dispatches used a hyphenated selector that matches nothing; the query must be re-run against the unhyphenated label, or a label-values enumeration run first, before any error signature or first-anomaly timestamp exists.

Is productcatalogservice saturating? No CPU, memory, GC, thread-pool or connection-pool series was ever retrieved. A memory or connection-pool ceiling would explain a partial, oscillating error rate and would point at resource_exhaustion.

What are productcatalogservice's latency percentiles, and is the error fraction correlated with timeouts on an outbound call? This is the discriminator between dependency_latency and a local fault, and it was never measured.

Why do adservice and cartservice have no call-count series at all in this window? Absent denominators mean either traffic ceased or emission/scraping stopped — either is unexplained and could be upstream of, downstream of, or unrelated to the productcatalogservice errors.

Was there any change to productcatalogservice or its dependencies between 03:53 and 04:43? Both change dispatches covered only the 15-minute window straddling onset; the preceding hour named in the original question is unqueried, and no dependency change stream was ever pulled.
Are the errors concentrated on a subset of replicas or pods? A per-instance breakdown would separate a bad artifact on some replicas from a fleet-wide condition, and no dispatch attempted it.
What is on the unmeasured edge that triage flagged, and does the causal path run through it? Nothing in the dispatch set probed beyond the instrumented boundary.
